clue.text: An armed timing device

parts.note: 'armed' suggests weaponry, but the timepiece is simply strapped to an arm, worn just above the hand

explanation.surface: A time bomb or similar weapon fitted with a detonator clock.
explanation.definitionFit: This timepiece is worn on the arm, so it is literally an armed timing device.

clue.text: With new income around, company becomes viable

indicators.note: around says the rearranged letters are wrapped about the abbreviation for company
new signals that the letters of income are made over into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A firm that gains fresh revenue becomes a going concern.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' makes ENOMIC; 'around' wraps it about the company abbreviation, which sits after the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Something economic pays its way, so a commercially viable scheme is an economic one.

clue.text: I'm getting information about love from her

parts.note: taken as written, without the apostrophe
love is zero in tennis scoring, the letter O
gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: Someone learns news of romance from a woman friend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting' and 'about' are only link words here, not a container signal; 'her' is the definition, a girl's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Imogen is a girl's name, the heroine of Shakespeare's Cymbeline, so it is a fair stand-in for a woman.

clue.text: An Inuit is likely to see one close up

definitions.text: An Inuit is likely to see one
definitions.meaning: an animal often met on Arctic ice, hunted by the Inuit
to shut tight or make airtight, as an envelope is shut

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a marine mammal of the Arctic and a verb meaning to shut something tight.

clue.text: Part of the film scenery that may be rented out

definitions.text: Part of the film scenery that may be rented out

parts.words: Part of the film scenery that may be rented out
parts.note: read as a movie set it is a painted canvas piece in a film building; read again it is a one-room home offered to tenants

explanation.surface: A piece of stage set from a film is hired out after shooting.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-room apartment, yet the words also suggest a flat (a scenery panel) in a film studio.

clue.text: Drink from the basin

indicators.note: from says the drink is made out of the letters of the basin, rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone sips liquid straight out of a washbasin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' is the anagram signal: the drink is made from the letters of THE BASIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Absinthe is a strong anise-flavoured spirit, a drink.

clue.text: Transport for student with a university final

indicators.note: final says the university's letter comes at the very end

parts.note: L is a learner, from the L-plate a learner driver displays
and means with, as in 'tea and cake'
taken as written

explanation.surface: A vehicle provided for a student taking end-of-year exams.
explanation.walkthrough: 'final' places U last, after L, AND and A.
explanation.definitionFit: A landau is a four-wheeled horse-drawn carriage, a form of transport.

clue.text: Assistance for the man with a record

parts.note: he is the pronoun for a man
an LP is a long-playing record

explanation.surface: A man brings along a vinyl album as his contribution.
explanation.definitionFit: Help and assistance are direct synonyms.

clue.text: Posh doctor living in modern flat

indicators.note: living in says one piece resides within another

parts.note: recent means modern, of late
U means upper-class, posh
MB is Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's degree

explanation.surface: A snobbish medic has an apartment in a new block.
explanation.walkthrough: 'living in' signals the container. 'flat' looks like a home, but is the adjective meaning lying down.
explanation.definitionFit: Recumbent means lying down, so it means flat, prone.

clue.text: An oar for a cutter

definitions.meaning: the broad flat end of a rowing oar
the sharp edge of a knife or sword

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both the flat paddle end of an oar and the cutting edge of a knife.

clue.text: Country seen differently by returned convict

indicators.note: differently says the letters of seen are put another way
returned means the word for convict is read backwards

parts.note: a lag is slang for a convict

explanation.surface: A released prisoner sees his homeland with new eyes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'differently' turns SEEN into SENE; 'returned' turns LAG into GAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Senegal is a nation of West Africa.

clue.text: Forgot the lines in production

parts.note: actors' slang for an actor whose memory fails on stage during a show

explanation.surface: An actor blanked on stage during the play.
explanation.definitionFit: In theatre slang an actor who forgets the script is said to have dried, gone silent.

clue.text: Females bringing endless anguish to the opposite sex

indicators.note: endless means the last letter of the anguish word is cut off

parts.note: woe is anguish
from the females' point of view, the opposite sex is males

explanation.surface: Women cause men no end of heartache.
explanation.definitionFit: Women are adult females, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Reverse order

definitions.meaning: a complete change of direction or opinion
a military drill command to face the other way

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a drill command to face the opposite way and, by extension, any reversal of policy.

clue.text: Relation without a tan in summer

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside: the relation word goes round the tan

parts.note: an account is a relation, a narrative
taken as written

explanation.surface: A family member came home from the holidays pale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of outside, and 'a' is a link. 'summer' is one who sums, not the season.
explanation.definitionFit: A summer, read as one who does sums, is a person who adds up figures for a living.

clue.text: Barge in exclusive circle in club

parts.note: narrow means restricted, exclusive

indicators.note: in says the circle goes inside the club

parts.note: a bat is a club used in cricket or baseball
a circle is shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone forces their way into a select clique at a club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Barge' looks like a verb (barge in) but is the boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrowboat is the slim canal boat of British waterways, a type of barge.

clue.text: He extends a hand at journey's end

definitions.text: He extends a hand at journey's end

parts.words: He extends a hand at journey's end
parts.note: the hand held out looks like a welcome, but it is held out for the passenger's travel pass at the barrier

explanation.surface: Someone greets a traveller with a handshake on arrival.
explanation.definitionFit: A railway official holds out a hand at the exit to take passengers' travel passes.

clue.text: Notice, in flight, a lark

indicators.note: in says the notice sits inside the flight word

parts.note: escape means flight, fleeing
an ad is a notice, an advertisement

explanation.surface: A notice that a lark has taken wing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lark' looks like the bird, set up by 'flight', but means a prank.
explanation.definitionFit: An escapade is a madcap adventure, a lark or prank.

clue.text: Gets mail out, but not without delays

indicators.note: out means the letters of gets mail are put out of order

explanation.surface: Post arrives, but late.
explanation.definitionFit: Time-lags are intervals between cause and effect, delays.

clue.text: Difficult to make love other than on grass

parts.note: hard means difficult
to court is to woo, in the old sense of make love

explanation.surface: Romance is tricky away from the lawn.
explanation.definitionFit: A tennis surface of asphalt or clay is played on instead of grass.

clue.text: Sharp practice produces outcry

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a fraudulent scheme and a loud noise or commotion.

clue.text: Arrived with nothing, but got relief

parts.note: came means arrived
nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone turned up empty-handed and felt eased.
explanation.walkthrough: 'relief' is carving in relief, not comfort.
explanation.definitionFit: A cameo is a small carving raised in relief against a background.

clue.text: Study and study non-English author

parts.note: to con is to study, learn by heart

indicators.note: non-English means E, for English, is removed

parts.note: to read a subject is to study it at university

explanation.surface: A reader pores over a foreign writer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'non-English' takes E from READ, leaving RAD.
explanation.definitionFit: Joseph Conrad was a Polish-born author who wrote in English.

clue.text: Kitty puts flag on vessel

parts.note: a jack is a ship's flag
a pot is a vessel

explanation.surface: Someone sticks a pennant on a jar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'puts on' places the flag first. 'Kitty' is the money pool, not a cat.
explanation.definitionFit: A jackpot is the pool of prize money, a kitty.

clue.text: Barely deserved

explanation.definitionFit: The word means 'only by a whisker' as an adverb and 'fair, deserved' as an adjective.

clue.text: Ardent followers form society on the blower

indicators.note: on says the society comes after the blower

parts.note: a fan blows air
a club is a society

explanation.surface: Keen supporters form an association, chatting by telephone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the blower' is British slang for the telephone, but here is a fan.
explanation.definitionFit: A fan club is an organised body of devoted admirers.

clue.text: Fuel designed to deal with smoke problem

indicators.note: designed means the letters of fuel are worked into a new design

explanation.surface: Fuel made to burn without smoke.
explanation.definitionFit: A chimney duct exists to carry smoke away, dealing with the problem.

clue.text: The going rate for amphetamine?

definitions.meaning: the pace or rate at which something goes

explanation.definitionFit: The word means velocity, a rate of going, and is street slang for amphetamine.

clue.text: Broken rule again leads to complaint

indicators.note: broken signals the letters of rule again are broken up and reset

explanation.surface: A repeated rule-breaker ends up with a grievance.
explanation.definitionFit: Neuralgia is nerve pain, a medical complaint.
